recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any future desire to make Substance support both instance and definition semantics again should be handled as a new policy change or a FHIR-48405 follow-up, not as a FHIR-29265 fixup.
issue_request: FHIR-29265 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and requested a mandatory boolean Substance.instance flag, true for instance and false for definition, with a Jira comment saying the new element would be an isModifier property.
initial_application: The request was explicitly applied in ce7d94f0984ae009254c17c60df0d81252aafac0, which cited FHIR#29265 and added the R5 Substance.instance flag while applying companion Substance changes from FHIR-29267 and FHIR-28547. FHIR-31526 later reverted breaking Substance changes for the R4B line, and subsequent R5 work restored the intended R5 Substance model.
additional_context: FHIR-48405 is a later Applied/Persuasive BR&R decision for R6 that removes Substance.instance, makes Substance only for instances, and directs definitions to SubstanceDefinition. The combined branch already contains FHIR-48405 reconciliation commit 1266a70e30373662bcaf36d0e1d4daf8a59f7c1f, plus related FHIR-29267 and FHIR-31526 audit commits. Substance is active in source/fhir.ini, and the remaining Substance.instance strings there are migration notes for old paths.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Reintroducing Substance.instance would now contradict the later approved Substance/SubstanceDefinition split, and the current authoritative source already conveys the implementer-significant distinction that motivated FHIR-29265.
